tells: 1. Front row reads as a mannequin line-up: nearly every front-table patron has the same forearms-on-table, hands-clasped pose, all squared to camera, at the same height (club-1-wide.png, front row across the whole lower half)

2. The laugh barely builds: from t=12.0 to 12.4 no-one changes, then by 13.0 only small head turns and the blonde woman's mouth opens. There's no visible wave through the room, and the back rows stay frozen in every frame (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, back rows and right half)

3. Face close is dead behind the eyes: the open mouth isn't matched by raised cheeks or crinkled eyes, the skin is waxy and evenly lit, and the hairline reads as a bare scalp cap (club-4-face.png, centre face and top of head)

4. The rear rows are uniform standing silhouettes with no rim light or motion, so they read as cardboard cut-outs filling space, not people (club-1-wide.png and club-2-mid.png, upper-middle band in front of the bar)
5. Hands and forearms pass into or float over the tabletops, and the white-sweater woman's lean looks forced over the table edge (club-6-held.png, centre-right table; club-3-mid.png, centre table)

1. The second row and the side figures look like they're standing or floating, not seated: torsos stack straight above the front row, and the left-aisle figures stand upright with arms hanging (theatre-1-wide.png, second row centre and far-left aisle at x~50-130)

2. The front row sits in one identical pose: knees apart, hands on knees, upright, the same for all eight. Wide and held frames are almost identical apart from two people, so the room looks frozen (theatre-1-wide.png vs theatre-6-held.png, front row)

3. The laugh lands in sync and abruptly: frames 12.0-12.6 are static, then four front-row mouths snap wide open together at 12.8-13.0 while the second row doesn't react at all (theatre-5-strip.png, bottom row frames; theatre-2-mid.png, front row)

4. Open-mouth shapes read as a shout or scream, with no cheek raise or eye squint. In the face close, the splayed long-nailed hand and neutral eyes give an uncanny 'pose' look (theatre-4-face.png, centre face and hand; theatre-2-mid.png, teal and brown-jacket women)

5. Low-poly silhouettes and a bad slump: polygonal sleeve and jacket edges in the close, a red glow bleeding off the left man, and the beanie man folded head-down so he reads as asleep (theatre-4-face.png, left background arm; theatre-3-mid.png, left red-shirt man and bottom-right beanie man)
1. The front row leans forward in unison, with hands on knees and the same forward hunch for all eight, so it looks like a choreographed row (openmic-1-wide.png, front row across the lower half)

2. Hair alpha and stipple artefacts: dithered and serrated hair-card edges on the yellow-shirt man and a visible cap edge on the afro man, which are very noticeable in closes (openmic-4-face.png, top-right of head; openmic-6-held.png, top of the afro and yellow-shirt man's hair)

3. Laughing mouths are dark voids or flat teeth and the eyes don't join the laugh. The green-shirt woman's upward gape looks like a scream (openmic-2-mid.png, centre green-shirt woman and short-hair woman)

4. The short-hair woman leans into the green-shirt woman until their shoulders and arms overlap, a likely interpenetration, while the yellow-shirt man stays exactly the same through the whole laugh (openmic-5-strip.png, frames 12.6-13.0, centre pair and yellow shirt)

5. Flat, uniform warm fill: no stage spill and no separation between the rows, so the back rows merge into a brown mass. The bright door panel and the green exit sign pull the eye (openmic-1-wide.png, back rows and door panel at upper-left; openmic-3-mid.png, background)
